newsitem.title: FRANCE: Far right defeated in French local election.
newsitem.headline: Far right defeated in French local election.

text.p: France's anti-immigration National Front lost in a local election on Sunday to ruling conservatives in the town of Dreux, west of Paris, with backing from opposition Socialists.

The defeat came as a blow to National Front leader Jean-Marie Le Pen, who had visited Dreux to help boost the local election campaign in the town, where his far-right party scored its first breakthrough in politics in 1983.
Mayor Gerard Hamel won 60.4 percent of the vote while National Front candidate Marie-France Stirbois trailed with 39.4 percent in the second and final round of voting, officials said.
"Dreux now has a new voice. People have said that they do not want hatred and exclusion here, and democracy has come out on top," Hamel said in his victory speech.
Gaullist Prime Minister Alain Juppe sent Hamel a message of congratulations, saying he represented values on which the nation should unite.

Conservative and Front supporters clashed in the streets after the results were announced. Local officials said no one was seriously injured but a Front spokesman said one of its supporters had been stabbed in the back and taken to hospital.
Opposition Socialists urged supporters to rally behind Hamel to defeat the Front after Stirbois topped the poll in the town of 36,000 people in last Sunday's first round with 36.5 percent.
She was closely followed by Hamel with 34.7 percent.
Socialist Maurice Ravanne, whose united Left list came third with 24.8 percent, agreed he would not to contest the run-off in a move calculated to swing the election for Hamel.
In her campaign, Stirbois said immigrants intimidated "native French people" and took their jobs. She also pledged to give the local police paramilitary training.

The Front last year won control of the southern towns of Toulon, Orange and Marignane, boosted by voter disenchantment with both mainstream blocs, accused of corruption and failure to halt unemployment and crime.
